## Appearance

Captain Jim was a tall, ungainly man, somewhat stooped in his old age, with a clean-shaven, deeply lined, and bronzed face. He possessed a thick mane of iron-gray hair that fell quite to his shoulders, and remarkably deep-set blue eyes that often looked out to sea. Although he considered himself plain-looking, his face was beautified by his cheerful, gentle, and radiant spirit.

_Sources: [v4 c6 P10](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0010), [v4 c6 P14](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0014), [v4 c6 P15](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0015), [v4 c9 P5](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0005)_

## Personality

Captain Jim was a simple-minded, high-souled, and gentle man with eternal youth in his heart. He possessed an unflagging cheerfulness and a quaint, practical wisdom, often observing that he had contracted a habit of enjoying everything. A natural and gifted storyteller, he delighted in sharing yarns of his seafaring days and held a deep reverence for beauty, nature, and true friendship. He was exceptionally kind-hearted, incapable of cruelty to animals, and fiercely protective of women, refusing to allow any unkind word about them in his presence.

_Sources: [v4 c6 P10](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0010), [v4 c6 P14](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0014), [v4 c6 P27](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0027), [v4 c9 P38](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0038), [v4 c9 P49](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0049), [v4 c9 P59](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0059), [v4 c17 P16](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0016), [v4 c17 P18](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0018)_

## History

Captain Jim was raised at Four Winds, Prince Edward Island, and ran away to sea as a boy, spending over fifty years sailing the globe. In his youth he loved a girl named Margaret, who tragically perished at sea during a squall, a loss that led him to remain unmarried for the rest of his life. In his later years he retired from the sea and became the keeper of the Four Winds Light, living a quiet life at the Point with his cat, the First Mate. He welcomed Dr. Gilbert Blythe and Anne Shirley when they moved into the nearby 'house of dreams,' instantly recognizing them as 'kindred spirits.' Captain Jim shared his vast store of sea yarns and his written 'life-book' with Owen Ford, a visiting author, who collaborated with him to turn the manuscript into a published book. Shortly after receiving his advance copy of the published book, Captain Jim passed away peacefully in his sleep at the lighthouse, holding his completed life-book.

_Sources: [v4 c5 P1](../source/v04-c05.md#nw-v04-c05-p0001), [v4 c6 P10](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0010), [v4 c7 P28](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0028), [v4 c7 P59](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0059), [v4 c9 P46](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0046), [v4 c17 P19](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0019), [v4 c20 P12](../source/v04-c20.md#nw-v04-c20-p0012), [v4 c25 P5](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0005), [v4 c39 P5](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0005), [v4 c39 P25](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0025), [v4 c39 P28](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0028)_

## Background by volume

- Ran away to sea as a young boy and spent most of his life sailing the world  <sub>[v4 c6 P10](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0010), [v4 c7 P28](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0028), [v4 c9 P46](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0046)</sub>
